In 가 and 방, the initial consonants ㄱ and ㅂ sit to the left of the vertical vowel ㅏ.
나 places ㄴ beside ㅏ; 무 places ㅁ above ㅜ.
바다 has two left-to-right blocks. The initial consonants ㅂ and ㄷ are different symbols.
In 사, ㅅ is the initial consonant and ㅏ is the vowel to its right.
차 is one syllable block: initial ㅊ followed by the vertical vowel ㅏ.
In 코, initial ㅋ sits above the horizontal vowel ㅗ.
아 and 이 begin with silent ㅇ. Their vertical vowels ㅏ and ㅣ sit to its right.
우 and 유 place silent initial ㅇ above the horizontal vowels ㅜ and ㅠ.
In 오, ㅗ sits below ㅇ; in 이, ㅣ sits to its right.
어 contains the vertical vowel ㅓ, whose short stroke extends to the left.
지 uses the vertical vowel ㅣ beside ㅈ; 도 uses the horizontal vowel ㅗ below ㄷ.
Both 구 and 두 place an initial consonant above the horizontal vowel ㅜ.
병 contains ㅕ, a vertical vowel with two short strokes on its left.

language_specific.lexical_frame: 우리 집: our home; often used for one's own home.

의 contains the compound vowel ㅢ, written with ㅡ below ㅇ and ㅣ to the right.

language_specific.pronunciation: Target: 회사 [회사] or [훼사]. Both pronunciations are standard.

language_specific.script_note: For ㄴ in 누나, write downward first, then continue the bottom stroke to the right.

For ㅗ in 모, write the short vertical stroke downward, then write the horizontal stroke from left to right.
For ㅜ in 두부, write the horizontal stroke from left to right, then the short vertical stroke downward.

common.meaning: please pack it to take away

language_specific.morphology: 포장하- + -여 forms 포장해; 주- + -세요 forms 주세요. Together 포장해 주세요 is a polite request based on 포장해 주다.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 김밥 포장해 주세요: ask for gimbap to be packed to take away.

language_specific.morphology: 영업하- + -여요 contracts to 영업해요, the informal polite form of 영업하다.
모르- + -아요 forms 몰라요: the 르 irregular pattern adds ㄹ to the preceding syllable and changes 르 to 라.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 그 단어는 몰라요: I do not know that word.

language_specific.morphology: 이해 + 못하다 forms the dictionary phrase 이해 못하다. In the sentence, 못하- + -였어요 contracts to 못했어요.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 설명을 이해 못했어요: I did not understand the explanation.

language_specific.social_context: The speaker respectfully asks the other person their name.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 성함이 어떻게 되세요?: a respectful way to ask someone's name.

language_specific.morphology: 어느 + 나라 + 에서: 에서 attaches to 나라 and marks the place of origin with 오다.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 어느 나라에서 왔어요?: which country are you from?
화장실이 어디예요?: where is the restroom?

language_specific.morphology: 배우- + -어요 contracts to 배워요, the informal polite form of 배우다.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 한국어를 배우다: learn Korean.
한국어를 조금 해요: I speak a little Korean.
아직 어려워요: it is still difficult.

language_specific.morphology: 돕- + -아 주다 forms 도와주다 through the ㅂ irregular pattern; 도와주- + -세요 forms 도와주세요.

common.note: A conventional way to accept an offer of something.

language_specific.morphology: 네 + 주- + -세요 forms 네, 주세요; 주세요 is the polite request form of 주다.

common.note: A conventional polite way to decline an offer.

language_specific.morphology: 아니요 + 괜찮- + -아요 forms 아니요, 괜찮아요; 괜찮아요 is the informal polite form of 괜찮다.

language_specific.social_context: A customer gets someone's attention before asking to pay.

common.note: A conventional request for someone to wait briefly.

language_specific.social_context: The speaker asks a staff member to wait briefly.

language_specific.lexical_frame: 영수증 주세요: please give me the receipt.

language_specific.morphology: 쓰- + -어 주다 forms 써 주다, with ㅡ dropped; 주- + -세요 forms 주세요.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 여기에 써 주세요: please write it here.

language_specific.morphology: 보이- + -어 주다 forms 보여 주다 by contraction; 주- + -세요 forms 주세요.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 주소를 보여 주세요: please show me the address.

common.note: A conventional farewell said to someone who is leaving.

language_specific.morphology: 안녕히 + 가- + -세요 forms 안녕히 가세요, a farewell using 가다.
language_specific.social_context: The speaker says goodbye to a departing teacher.

common.note: A conventional farewell said by someone who is leaving.

language_specific.morphology: 안녕히 + 계시- + -어요 forms 안녕히 계세요; 계시다 is the honorific verb for staying.
language_specific.social_context: The speaker says goodbye to 사장님 while leaving; the addressee remains.

language_specific.morphology: 또 + 뵈- + -어요 contracts to 또 봬요; 뵈다 is a humble verb for seeing or meeting someone.
language_specific.social_context: A learner tells a teacher they will meet again tomorrow.

language_specific.morphology: 좋은 하루 + 보내- + -세요 forms 좋은 하루 보내세요, using 보내다 for spending a day.
한국어 + 로: 로 attaches to the vowel-final noun 한국어 and marks the language used.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 한국어로 뭐예요?: what is it in Korean?

language_specific.morphology: 영어 + 로: 로 attaches to the vowel-final noun 영어 and marks the language used.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 영어로 말하다: speak in English.

language_specific.morphology: 역 + 에: 에 attaches to 역 and marks the destination.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 역에 가다: go to the station.

language_specific.morphology: 주- + -세요 → 주세요.
카드 + 로: 로 attaches to the vowel-final noun 카드 and marks the means of payment.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 카드로 결제하다: pay by card.

language_specific.morphology: 보- + -ㄹ 수 있다 + -을까요 forms 볼 수 있을까요, a polite question about possibility.
language_specific.social_context: A customer politely asks to see the menu.
language_specific.lexical_frame: 메뉴를 볼 수 있을까요?: could I see the menu?

common.note: A conventional polite remark when parting after a meeting.

language_specific.morphology: 만나- + -아서 contracts to 만나서; 반갑- + -었어요 forms 반가웠어요 through the ㅂ irregular pattern.
